name: Montréal, Canada 🇨🇦
subtitle: The most underrated food city in North America
items: Au Pied de Cochon (Martin Picard, Plateau-Mont-Royal — foie gras poutine, duck in a can, the maximalist icon)
Joe Beef (David McMillan + Frédéric Morin, Little Burgundy — lobster spaghetti, natural wine, impossible reservation)
Liverpool House (same team as Joe Beef, next door — slightly easier to get in)
Le Vin Papillon (Joe Beef crew's wine bar, vegetable-focused, natural wine — special)
Toqué! (Normand Laprise, Old Montreal — the modern Québécois anchor, since 1993)
Schwartz's Deli (The Main, since 1928 — smoked meat sandwich, mustard, pickle, que always)
Beauty's Luncheonette (Mount Royal Ave, since 1942 — the breakfast. Mish-mash plate is the order)
Fairmount Bagel (Mile End, since 1919 — wood-fired, honey-water, better than Montreal's other famous bagel)
St-Viateur Bagel (Mile End, since 1957 — the other great bagel, the debate never ends)
Elena (Mile End, Ryan Gray + Marysol Foucault — pizza + natural wine, the cool-kid spot)
Lawrence (Mile End, Marc Cohen — British cooking, seasonal, Sunday roast legend)
Comptoir Charcuteries et Vins (Plateau, small plates + charcuterie)
Dépanneur Le Pick Up (Mile End, the gourmet corner store that serves plates)
Wilensky's Light Lunch (Mile End, since 1932 — the special sandwich on a pressed bun, cash only)
Le Fantôme (Griffintown, natural wine + small plates)
Foxy (Plateau, Leigh Roper — brunch royalty)
Pastel (Mile End, pastel-colored, photogenic, great food)
Hoogan et Beaumont (Rosemont, neighbourhood French)
Olive + Gourmando (Old Montreal, since 1997 — best café in the city)
Mess Hall (NDG, casual but excellent)
